text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
England's KING GEORGE III, whose mishandling of the American
colonies was responsible for the War Of Independence, was born
in 1738. He reigned from 1760 until he became insane in 1811,
when the Prince of Wales was appointed regent.
American composer STEPHEN FOSTER, who wrote "Swanee River",
was born in 1826.
Australian writer BARBARA BAYNTON, who was married three
times (the last time to BARON HEADLEY, whom she left when he
refused the throne of Albania) was born in 1857.
Australian aeronautical engineer LESLIE JONES, who designed
the 'Wonga' aircraft and later worked on the 'Gannet' and
'Mosquito' bomber, was born in 1886. Australian artist HAROLD
ABBOT was born in 1906.
American actress ROSALIND RUSSELL, who appeared in film and
Broadway dramas and musicals including "Night Must Fall", was
born in 1908.
High profile Methodist Minister ALLAN WALKER, who founded
the telephone crisis service Life-Line, was born in 1911.
American singer and songwriter FREDDY FENDER (born BALDEMAR
HUERTA in Mexico), who had hits with "Before The Next Teardrop
Falls" and "Wasted Days And Wasted Nights", was born in 1937.
British singer CLIFF BENNETT, who had a hit with "Got To Get
You Into My Life" (1966), was born in 1940.
Australian guitarist ROB E. G., who was born ROB E. PORTER
and went on to become very successful in the American music
industry, was born in 1942.
British singer/guitarist GORDON WALLER ("Peter and Gordon"),
who had a hit with "I Go To Pieces" (1965), was born in 1945.
British 'session' drummer PETER VAN HOOKE, who played with
several artists including VAN MORRISON and SHEENA EASTON, was
born in 1950.
US leadsinger and keyboard player with the family group 'De
Barge', EL De BARGE was born in 1962. Hits included "Rhythm Of
The Night" (1985), "Who's Holding Donna Now" (1985) and "Who's
Johnny" (1986) from the film 'Short Circuit'.
** EVENTS **
1798 : The man claimed to have been one of the world's
greatest lovers, Italian GIOVANNI GIACOMO CASANOVA DE SEINGALT
died. He was also a spy in the Venetian Police Force, a
violinist and librarian.
1805 : The first ceremony of the Trooping of the Colour
was staged in Horse Guards Parade in London.
1844 : Scientists discovered a 'great auk' in Iceland.
The large, flightless bird (a marine-diving bird that used its
wings to 'fly' underwater) was thought to have been extinct. It
was extinct soon after.
1926 : Australian cricketer FREDERICK SPOFFORTH, known as
"the demon bowler", died.
1937 : The first supermarket trolley was pushed down the
aisles of a store in Oklahoma.
1970 : The British protectorate of Tonga became
independent within the Commonwealth.
1988 : The first Aborigine to govern a State (South
Australia) and receive a knighthood, Pastor SIR DOUGLAS RALPH
NICHOLLS, died at the age of 81.
1940 : British Prime Minister WINSTON CHURCHILL made his
famous "We shall fight on the beaches... we shall never
surrender" speech to the House of Commons.
1941 : Kaiser WILHELM II, ninth king of Prussia and third
German emperor from 1888-1918, died in exile in the Netherlands.
1944 : Rome was liberated by Allied Forces.
1946 : General JUAN PERON was inaugurated as president of
Argentina.
1989 : The Chinese Army stormed Tiananmen Square in
Beijing to remove protesting students, reportedly killing up to
2,600 people and injuring thousands more, in an attempt to crush
the growing pro-democracy movement. The world was soon to be
flooded with visions of lone students defiantly standing before
tanks and openly attacking the Government forces. Tiananmen
Square is the largest public square in the world, covering
almost half a square kilometre.
1989 : Around 800 people were thought to have died in a
massive gas explosion that wrecked two crowded passenger trains
on the Trans-Siberian railway. Leaking gas from a huge,
long-distance pipeline running beside the tracks, was ignited by
sparks as the trains passed. The surrounding forest was reduced
to cinders in the resulting explosion, yet one of the injured
train drivers managed to crawl to a nearby village to alert
authorities to the disaster.
1993 : The U.N. Security Council agreed to send armed
troops to Bosnia to protect six "safe havens" -- Sarajevo,
Tuzla, Zepa, Srebrenica, Gorazde and Bihac.
1996 : Europe's Ariane-5 rocket was blown up by ground
controllers after it veered off course 40 seconds into its
maiden flight.
